formMetadata.purpose: Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, is filed by an alien physically present in the United States to request adjustment of their immigration status to that of a lawful permanent resident under various provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act.
formMetadata.situations: Filed by individuals eligible under INA §245(a) (general adjustment), §245(i) (penalty provision for grandfathered aliens), §245(j) (investor-based), §245(m) (U nonimmigrant crime victims), §209(a)/(b) (refugee/asylee adjustment), §249 (registry), the Cuban Adjustment Act, Section 13 of the Act of September 11, 1957, CSPA, VAWA, and numerous special statutory programs. Covers family-based (immediate relatives and preference categories), employment-based (EB-1 through EB-5), special immigrants (SIJ, religious workers, Afghan/Iraqi nationals), diversity visa, asylee/refugee adjustment, T/U nonimmigrant adjustment, and other special programs. Applicants must generally be physically present in the U.S. and have been inspected and admitted or paroled, unless filing under §245(i) or an exempt category.
formMetadata.use-cases: 1) Spouse of U.S. citizen with approved I-130 adjusts status. 2) EB-2 worker with approved I-140 and current priority date. 3) Asylee adjusts one year after asylum grant under INA §209(b). 4) Refugee adjusts one year after admission under INA §209(a). 5) Diversity visa lottery winner adjusts before fiscal year ends. 6) U visa holder adjusts after 3 years continuous physical presence. 7) T visa holder adjusts under INA §245(l). 8) VAWA self-petitioner adjusts with approved I-360. 9) Special Immigrant Juvenile with approved I-360. 10) K-1 fiancé(e) marries USC and adjusts within 90 days. 11) Cuban national adjusts under Cuban Adjustment Act. 12) Derivative child or spouse files concurrently with principal applicant. 13) Applicant with prior unlawful presence files under §245(i).
formMetadata.filing-context: I-485 is the central adjustment of status application. Commonly filed concurrently with I-130 (immediate relative petition), I-765 (EAD), I-131 (Advance Parole), I-693 (medical examination, sealed), I-864/I-864EZ (Affidavit of Support), and I-130A (supplemental info for spouse). Supporting evidence includes passport copies, birth certificates, photos, civil documents, I-94 records, I-797 approval notices, police clearances, and court dispositions. Filed at USCIS lockbox or online via myUSCIS. For EOIR filings, submitted directly to the immigration judge. Edition 01/20/25; OMB expires 10/31/2027.
formMetadata.parties-involved: Applicant: The individual applying for adjustment to lawful permanent resident status; provides all biographical data, immigration history, and answers all eligibility/inadmissibility questions. Petitioner: The U.S. citizen, LPR, or employer who filed the underlying immigrant petition; referenced but not a direct party on I-485. Interpreter: Translates the application for the applicant; completes Part 11. Preparer: Prepares the form on the applicant's behalf; completes Part 12. USCIS Officer: Adjudicating officer who conducts the interview and administers the oath in Part 13.
